title: A Microfluidic Platform for Longitudinal Imaging in Caenorhabditis elegans
protocol: Mount the microfluidic device on an inverted fluorescence microscope with a motorized stage.
Place an orbital shaker close to the microscope ensuring it does not vibrate the microscope directly.
Fix the syringe pump to the orbital shaker using tape to prevent movement during shaking.
Prepare an outlet syringe and a syringe tube for connection to the microfluidic device's outlet.
Make an adapter needle by removing plastic parts of a 20 G x 1/2 inch syringe tip.
Hold the plastic and metal parts with pliers and pull them apart.
Burn off remaining plastic residue on the needle with a Bunsen burner.
Bend the needle to an angle of ~110° in its middle using pliers.
Plug the adapter needle halfway into the tube.
Connect a 10 mL luer-lock syringe to the other (open) end of the syringe tube via a 20 G x 1/2 inch syringe tip.
Prepare buffer-inlet syringes and syringe tubes.
Connect one 10 mL luer-lock syringe (S2) directly to a 3-way valve.
Connect another 10 mL luer-lock syringe (S3) to the same valve via a syringe tube.
Connect a syringe tube to the remaining port of the 3-way valve.
Prepare another adapter needle and plug it halfway into the other end of the syringe tube.
Set the valve such that the syringe tube from Step 2.2.2 and S2 are connected while S3 is closed.
Prepare a worm-inlet syringe (S4) and connect a long syringe tube to a 10 mL luer-lock syringe.
Determine the length of the tubing based on the volume of fluid needed for loading.
Plug one half of an adapter needle into the other end of the syringe tube.
Rinse all syringes and tubing with S-medium twice.
Fill the syringes and tubes with S-medium, removing all air bubbles.
Connect the outlet syringe tube to the device outlet.
Inject a small volume of S-medium through the outlet to fill up the device until it comes out of both buffer inlet and worm inlet.
Plug in the adapter needle at the end of the syringe tube into the outlet port.
Connect the buffer-inlet syringe tube to the buffer-inlet port of the device.
Plug the worm-inlet with a pin.
Inject a constant flow of buffer into the device using syringe S2 at a flow rate of 3 µL/min.
Load Escherichia coli OP50 suspended in S-medium.
Inoculate a 250 mL flask with 50 mL of LB and a single colony, then incubate overnight at 37 °C.
Centrifuge the overnight culture at 4000 rpm for 10 minutes.
Resuspend the pellet in 30 mL of S-medium.
Filter the bacterial suspension through a 5 µm syringe filter.
Measure the optical density of the bacterial suspension at 600 nm (OD600).
Adjust the bacterial concentration to an OD600 of 3.
Prepare a clean syringe (S5) filled with the OP50 suspension.
Tap S5 vertically several times to collect air bubbles at the top.
Close the connection of buffer-inlet syringes to the device using the 3-way valve.
Disconnect S2 from the valve and connect S5 to the valve.
Push out all air collected in S5 through the valve until a little bit of OP50 suspension goes into S3.
Turn the 3-way valve back to the original position to close the connection between S3 and S5 and connect S5 to the device.
Load S5 onto the syringe pump.
Turn on the orbital shaker that holds the pump.
Set the shaking speed to approximately 200 rpm.
Set the flow rate to be 100 µL/min.
Prepare a small low binding microcentrifuge tube (650 μL) and fill it with 100 µL of OP50 suspension.
Transfer around 20 - 30 age-synchronized young adult worms from an NGM agar plate to the tube by picking them one by one with a worm pick.
Fill the worm-inlet syringe and syringe tube (S4) with the OP50 suspension.
Inject ~500 µL of the fluid into the microcentrifuge tube with worms.
Draw the suspension with worms into the worm-inlet syringe tube.
Connect S4 to the worm-inlet.
Inject all worms from the worm-inlet syringe tube into the microfluidic device.
Disconnect S4 and the syringe tube.
Plug the worm-inlet with a pin.
Disengage the buffer-inlet syringe S2 from the mechanical pump.
Manually control S1 and S2 to push worms into separate channels.
Press S2 to move worms into the channels.
Press S1 to move worms in the reverse direction if needed.
Let worms adjust to the new environment for 2 - 3 hours.
Find all worms securely located in the device.
Set an imaging position for each worm in the image acquisition software.
Load a text file listing positions where images should be taken, if using automated script.
Create a list of imaging positions with a small script (e.g., Python) as needed.
Set the frequency of time-lapse imaging.
Acquire all necessary channels at every time point.
Inoculate a 250 mL flask with 50 mL of LB and a single colony, then incubate overnight at 37 °C.
Inoculate another 250 mL flask with 50 mL of LB and an aliquot of the culture, then incubate overnight at 37 °C.
Centrifuge the overnight culture at 4000 rpm for 10 minutes.
Resuspend the pellet in 10 mL of SK-medium.
Measure the bacterial concentration and adjust to OD600 = 4.
Transfer the suspension to a clean flask, incubate at 37 °C for 24 hours, then continue incubation at 25 °C for another 24 hours while shaking.
Filter the suspension through a 5 μm syringe filter.
Replace the OP50 suspension in the device with the PA14 suspension using the same procedure as Step 3.2.
Keep imaging for 10 hours.
